Hi Asha / DataWave team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap, what we saw in the demo, and the minimal set of technical checks we agreed on so we can size a Private/VPC deployment and validate air-gap feasibility: 

1) Control plane connectivity: verify whether your environment supports a customer-initiated outbound-only control-plane handshake (no inbound routes). We can provide a short handshake test that runs from a bastion with no egress proxy.
2) Network egress policy & firewall rules: we need the specific FQDNs/IPs and ports for the control-plane endpoints and telemetry. If you prefer, we can produce an allowlist JSON for your firewall team.
3) Air-gap feasibility checklist: verify whether an update bundle process via removable media is acceptable (we outlined two options: managed update broker vs. sealed bundle).
4) Performance comparison: DataWave asked for a targeted perf/cost comparison vs. GCP Vertex endpoints on your representative workload — we will run a small benchmark (1000 short chat requests) to compare median p95 latency and tokens-per-dollar.
5) Security evidence: SOC2 artifacts + KMS/HSM integration notes. Monica will provide SOC2 evidence and an outline of our KMS options.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-networking-checklist.pdf (network checklist), datawave-controlplane-seq.png (sequence diagram), redwood-gcp-compare-onepager.pdf (benchmark template).

Next concrete steps I propose:
- Asha: share the network contact for a brief 30-min call to walk the checklist (we can do Wed or Thu this week).
- DataWave: confirm whether the environment must be fully air-gapped (no initial egress) or whether a scheduled, controlled egress window is acceptable for the initial bootstrap.
- Redwood: Karthik will prepare a control-plane handshake runbook; Monica will pull SOC2 evidence; Laura will surface preliminary pricing options and credits for an initial POC.

If that looks right, I’ll send calendar invites and the short playbook for the test.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We prefer outbound-only control plane if possible; our security team disallows inbound.
- For initial evaluation we cannot allow any persistent egress to public endpoints; we can accommodate a negotiated maintenance window for bootstrap (1 hour, outbound-only) if that simplifies the POC.
- Our network lead is Kevin Ortiz (kevin.ortiz@datawave.com). Please loop him for the checklist call.
- On compliance: we’re SOC2 Type II in progress and need to see encryption-in-transit and KMS integration details before legal will move forward.

Can your team share the allowlist JSON and a short note on how the update bundle would work in a fully air-gapped scenario? If you can do the benchmark vs GCP, please include expected VM families and a rough cost delta we should anticipate.

Thanks — Asha
CTO, DataWave Inc.

Asha — perfect, thanks for the details and for Kevin’s contact. 

- Outbound-only control plane is supported by our Private offering. Karthik will send the handshake runbook (small script + expected outbound endpoints) and an allowlist JSON you can hand to your firewall team.
- Air-gap: we support two paths — (A) sealed update bundles (signed archive delivered via removable media, validated by an HSM-backed signing key), or (B) a maintenance-window bootstrap where a ticketed outbound-only session fetches the initial images and KV cache. We’ll document both; Monica will attach the compliance notes for the signed-bundle flow.
- Benchmark plan: we’ll run the same inference workload you demo’d (50-token responses, beam=1) on a comparable GCP endpoint (n1-highmem equivalent) and on a Redwood Private node with quantization enabled. We’ll capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, and tokens-per-dollar. Expect initial delta of ~20–40% cost reduction when using our batching+KV caching on typical chat workloads, but we’ll validate empirically.

I’ll propose two times for the 30-min checklist call with Kevin: Thu 12/10 09:00-09:30 PT or Thu 12/10 13:00-13:30 PT. Which works?

Ben
